claims.text: Departures from individual randomization in a subsample of the PREDIMED trial did not cause clinically meaningful attenuation in the strength of its findings.
The results of the PREDIMED trial were robust across a wide range of sensitivity analyses.
The criteria for causality between the Mediterranean diet and cardiovascular health outcomes were met.
Better conformity with the traditional Mediterranean diet is associated with reductions in rates of coronary heart disease.
Better conformity with the traditional Mediterranean diet is associated with reductions in rates of ischemic stroke.
Better conformity with the traditional Mediterranean diet is associated with reductions in rates of total cardiovascular disease.

evidence.description: Some departures from individual randomization in a subsample of the landmark Spanish trial (PREDIMED [Prevención con Dieta Mediterránea]) did not represent any clinically meaningful attenuation in the strength of its findings.
The results of PREDIMED were robust in a wide range of sensitivity analyses.

The criteria for causality were met and potential sources of controversies did not represent any reason to compromise the main findings of the available observational studies and randomized controlled trials.
Better conformity with the traditional MedDiet is associated with better cardiovascular health outcomes, including clinically meaningful reductions in rates of coronary heart disease.
Better conformity with the traditional MedDiet is associated with better cardiovascular health outcomes, including clinically meaningful reductions in rates of ischemic stroke.
Better conformity with the traditional MedDiet is associated with better cardiovascular health outcomes, including clinically meaningful reductions in rates of total cardiovascular disease.

methodologies.name: Systematic Critical Review and Re-analysis
methodologies.description: Systematic review and critical assessment of prospective cohorts and randomized controlled trials included in 5 major meta-analyses published between 2014 and 2018 plus additional prospective studies evaluating MedDiet effects on hard cardiovascular end points.
conditions: Explicit reporting on MedDiet effect on hard cardiovascular end points

limitations.text: Methodological aspects of Mediterranean intervention trials and limitations in the quality of some meta-analyses raised recent controversies.
Departures from individual randomization occurred in a subsample of the PREDIMED trial.
